about: Design-production status for the low-fidelity wireframes, and nothing else. It says which surface is in which review batch, which artefacts exist, in which language and viewport, which states they cover and how far the review has gone. It restates no requirement: the surface, its rows and its states are in design/inventory/surfaces.json, and every entry here points at one by its canonical id. Checked by tools/design_wireframes.py. The format and the workflow are in README.md and workflow.md beside this file.

review_statuses.briefed: A brief is generated. Nothing is drawn.
review_statuses.exploration: Being explored in the calibration set or in its batch. More than one treatment may exist.

review_statuses.wireframed: Drawn in full: every listed state, both languages where they apply, mobile and desktop.

review_statuses.not_applicable: Not wireframed: a provider's interface, or a surface that exists only at high fidelity.

directions.label: Clean Premium Commerce
directions.approach: Calm and restrained. Lower density, generous whitespace, a quiet header, large product imagery, and merchandising content used sparingly so the product carries each view.

directions.label: Editorial Modern Retail
directions.approach: Composed like a publication. Larger editorial blocks set among the products, strong typographic hierarchy, imagery that dominates, and grids that vary rather than repeat.

directions.label: Dynamic Contemporary Ecommerce
directions.approach: Energetic and efficient. Higher density, more products in view, prominent merchandising rails and badges, a utility-forward header, and the purchase actions kept close at hand.

directions_note: The labels are descriptive only. They are three structural approaches to hierarchy, density, composition and interaction, not three brand identities. All three satisfy the same scope, draw the same states, keep every pattern the contract fixes, and stay neutral. They may differ only in presentation and in interaction choices that are genuinely open. None adds a feature.

calibration.purpose: Establish the structural ecommerce direction on a representative set of first-release customer surfaces, in three directions, before it is carried across the inventory. Exploration: it locks nothing until the owner selects.

reconfirmation.record: A deliberate review and approval of the final structural UX direction, after the selection above was first recorded in #353 (c139c45). The selection stands, and the fields above are kept as first recorded. Direction C is the structural baseline, with premium A-inspired restraint applied consistently across the full storefront. Not approval of the brand colours, the typography, the imagery, the high-fidelity interface or PRE-03b, not a client confirmation, and no change to the contracted scope.
reconfirmation.kept_from_c: The contemporary navigation, search, product discovery and filtering, the product detail architecture, the sticky desktop purchase area, the cart, the mini-cart and the checkout presentation.
reconfirmation.applied_throughout: Calmer hierarchy, purposeful whitespace, reduced visual clutter, restrained card treatment and product-led composition, on every storefront surface.
refinements: IX-02 is refined: a deliberate click or tap of the cart control opens the drawer, with focus managed and returned to the control that opened it; a successful quick add from a listing or a product rail is confirmed in place, updates the header count and is announced, without opening the drawer or moving focus away from the quick add; a failed add shows its error, with no success message and no change to the count; an add from the cart's suggestions does not automatically open another drawer. The confirmation after Add to Cart on the product page is IX-10, open for the batch-03 review: the owner allows the drawer there and has not chosen it.

IX-08 stands as recorded: the full description stays a tab (PDP-12), the key features and the purchase information are reachable without opening several tabs, and delivery, returns and authenticity are clearly reachable.

IX-09 stands: one prominent hero, never an autoplaying carousel. Category shortcuts (HOME-05) and the featured collections (HOME-04) are separate sections, and trending (HOME-02) and new arrivals (HOME-03) are separate, independently managed sections. Purposeful motion is allowed where it never obstructs shopping or costs performance.

The checkout stands: DQ-03's one page with C's presentation, every required review item before Place Order, the condensed header with the logo, search, account, wishlist, cart and language switcher, and no express delivery in the first release (SHIP-07, P2).
DQ-01 and DQ-02 stay provisional: Western digits and native numbered pagination are the working baselines, and Load More is not newly authorised.

Motion: purposeful microinteractions, accessible overlays and meaningful feedback; no compulsory carousel motion, no scroll-jacking and no animation that delays a purchase; reduced motion and mobile performance are design constraints. A Lighthouse score of 99 to 100 is an aspirational engineering target, not a contractual guarantee.

Account, batches 04 and 06: a coherent desktop sidebar and mobile account navigation, a dashboard with recent orders and their statuses, clear profile and password sections, and accurate verification, cart-merge, recovery and account-security states. The account audit and its signed-scope validation are planning references, not authority to change the inventoried states; the account's technical and scope decisions stay with those batch reviews and do not block batch-01.

open_decision.recommendation: Claude Design recommends confirming the add in place in the buy area: the button shows Adding, then a tick; a confirmation under it names the item, variant and quantity, with View cart and Checkout; the header count steps up on success only; one polite live announcement; focus stays on Add to cart; the mini-cart drawer opens only on a deliberate press of the header cart. A failed add shows its error in the same place, with role=alert, no count change and no add_to_cart event. Drawn in sf-pdp-simple (adding, added, from the mobile bar, and a failed add) and sf-pdp-variable (selected, no_selection).
open_decision.rationale: The visitor is still deciding on the product page; an inline confirmation keeps them there, follows the rule IX-02 already locks for quick adds, keeps focus where it was, and avoids stacking a drawer over the mobile buy bar. Cart and checkout stay one press away. The alternative, the mini-cart drawer as a focused confirmation, keeps the free-shipping prompt (CART-07) in view after an add, at the cost of a modal layer, moved focus and a second behaviour for the same action.
open_decision.not_a_lock: Recorded as a recommendation for the owner's batch-03 review. It is not a lock, and interaction-options.json is unchanged.
open_decision.alignment_pending: The inventory note on sf-pdp-simple:added reads "Mini-cart shown". It predates IX-10 and does not match the drawn recommendation. It is deliberately left unchanged in this import; the inventory and its brief need aligning once IX-10 is decided, whichever pattern is chosen.
open_decision.review_point: The in-page confirmation stays until the quantity changes or the visitor adds again. The confirmation on the mobile buy bar is drawn to return to one row when the visitor scrolls on, or after about five seconds without focus inside it. A keyboard user keeps it, since focus stays on the bar's Add to cart; a touch or screen-reader user who has not moved focus loses the View cart and Checkout links after five seconds, with the header cart as the remaining route. Whether the bar's confirmation should also persist, or collapse only on scroll, is part of the IX-10 decision. It has no close control, and a non-modal confirmation needs none.

Each frame was measured at the width it is drawn, from live layout: the page box's scrollWidth against its clientWidth; any element extending past the page box without a clipping container; every control's effective hit area, the element's box united with an absolutely positioned ::after where it has one, clipped to any scrolling or cropping container; and every pair of hit areas in the same frame, except a pair split by an open modal drawer, whose page is inert. Screenshots were not used for figures.
measurements.frames: Per language: 5 at 360 px, 82 at 390, 5 at 768, 2 at 1024 and 79 at 1280 (outer widths; the page inside is 2 px narrower), 173 in all, 346 across both languages.
measurements.overflow: 0 frames overflow horizontally at any width in either language, and 0 elements escape their page box unclipped. This includes sf-cart:long_content at 360 px in Arabic (five units, long names, five-digit prices) and au-register default and validation at 360 px in Arabic.
measurements.targets: 6,421 controls measured. Every one is at least 44 x 44 px except two inherited elements, both recorded under carried_findings: the batch-02 product-card name link (122 visible instances) and the batch-01 footer email field (4 instances). Overlapping hit areas: 0. The Arabic Remove line action, the consent labels, the Google button, Show and Hide, the steppers, the coupon disclosure and the drawer's close control all measure 44 px or more.
measurements.forms: au-register at 360 px: three 326 px fields in both languages, no overflow, smallest target 44 px, in default and in validation. au-sign-in at 390 px: two 356 px fields. The other authentication surfaces are drawn at 390 px and measure the same way: no overflow and no target under 44 px.
measurements.mini_cart_drawer: English opens at the inline end (right) and Arabic at the inline end (left), 0 px from the page edge, at 768 and 1280 px: 420 x 820 px. At 390 px it is full width and full height, 388 x 760 px, and 358 x 760 px at 360 px. The foot is pinned to the bottom of the drawer (0 px gap) in every open, empty, after_add and long_content frame. View cart and Checkout measure 138 x 46 and 234 x 46 px on tablet and desktop, 129 x 46 and 219 x 46 px at 390 px, and 118 x 46 and 200 x 46 px at 360 px. The long list is drawn clipped under the pinned foot with a drawn scrollbar; scrolling itself is a representation.
measurements.stylesheets: All five stylesheet links return 200 and parse (91, 262, 5, 138 and 152 rules) in all 30 files; the only failed request is the browser's own favicon probe. The reused batch-01 header and footer render with their styles, and the first footer list link measures 44 px through batch-02-targets.css.
measurements.checkout_bar: The mobile checkout bar is drawn once per language, in the sf-cart default first view at 390 px: 388 x 73 px, flush with the bottom of the 760 px cropped view, with a 48 px Checkout button. In English it covers no control. In Arabic, whose lines wrap taller, it sits over the third line's stepper and line actions: the picture of content scrolling under a sticky bar, not two controls in the same place. The bar is drawn with position absolute inside the crop; sticky behaviour, the reserved scroll padding that keeps a focused control clear of it, and hiding it while the keyboard or the cookie banner is open are annotated, not built.
measurements.not_built: Focus moving into the drawer and staying there, Escape and the return of focus, live announcements, and motion with its reduced-motion behaviour are documented requirements in the notes. The wireframes carry no script, so none of it functions here, and none of it was measured. Physical devices and final fonts were not measured.

source_differences.item: US-05-02 and the locked add confirmation
source_differences.status: The Functional Specification's first criterion for US-05-02 reads "Adding an item updates the header count and shows the mini cart". CART-12 says only "Mini-cart in header", and the locked IX-02 and IX-10 confirm an add in place without opening the drawer. The locked pattern governs the wireframe and is what is drawn. The difference is kept for formal reconciliation of the specification; the specification is not edited here.

Verified from the stepper quantities in every frame. The sample's not-qualified prompt, "Add 1 more item to get free shipping", appears in 39 frames per language on carts of two or more units: sf-cart (23 frames: default, updating, item_removed, moved_to_wishlist, coupon_applied, coupon_invalid, signed_out, signed_in, long_content), sf-cart-revalidation (8, all four states), sf-free-shipping-progress:default (3) and sf-mini-cart open and long_content (5), at 2, 3, 4, 5 and 8 units. The same sample is drawn as qualifying at 2 units (sf-free-shipping-progress:qualified), 3 units (sf-cart:free_shipping_applied, the same EGP 5,580 cart that sf-cart:default shows as not qualified) and 4 units (sf-mini-cart:after_add). Only the two sf-free-shipping-progress:not_qualified frames, at 1 unit, show the prompt consistently. So the sample contradicts the owner's working default (two or more units qualify) and also contradicts itself under any single threshold. The file's note that sample quantities are not evaluated against the default does not cure the internal contradiction. The prompt's wording is correctly drawn as a variable filled by the rule, and nothing hard-codes the number.
source_differences.proposed_correction: The smallest correction, for the owner to direct: in those 39 frames per language, replace the sample sentence and bar with a rule-neutral placement of the same component (the free-shipping prompt slot, labelled as sf-free-shipping-progress with its state and wording set by the rule, OD-04), keeping its position and keeping Shipping as "Calculated at checkout". Then only the frames that are about the state show one: not_qualified at 1 unit, and qualified, free_shipping_applied and after_add at 2 to 4 units, all consistent with the working default without stating a threshold. No business rule is fixed or locked by it. Changing the 39 frames to show free shipping instead would tie the sample to an unconfirmed default and is not proposed.
source_differences.closure: A focused correction is recommended before the batch closes. It is not made in this import, and the imported files are unchanged.

source_differences.status: The changed line is preserved as drawn: "Quantity changed from 3 to 2: the quantity we can confirm now", with plus unavailable and the wording marked PRE-09. No public stock count, "only N left", reservation, timing, sync rule or ERP fallback is drawn or inferred. A reduced quantity reveals a figure indirectly, which PRE-09's "no stock quantity shown to customers" may not allow; whether it may, and the wording, wait on PRE-09, as the batch-03 deferral "Quantity limit without a stock figure" already records.

provisional_assumptions.item: AUTH-02, registration with a phone number
provisional_assumptions.status: Drawn as an optional phone field on the email and password form, with no one-time code and no SMS verification. That is a provisional design assumption, not confirmed compliance. The signed row is "Register with phone number", P1-L, and P1-L means a reduced specification listed in Part One section 1.2, but section 1.2 lists no reduction for AUTH-02, so its launch boundary is undefined. Collecting an optional number is not the same as letting a customer register with a phone number: registration by phone makes the number an account identifier, and usually means proving the customer holds it, while SMS is INT-07 (P2, not contracted) and notifications are email only at launch.
provisional_assumptions.needs_clarification: What AUTH-02's reduced specification is; whether a phone number may be the identifier a customer registers and signs in with at launch, and if so how it is proved without SMS; and whether an optional phone field on email registration satisfies the row.

provisional_assumptions.status: The signed register describes it explicitly as a passwordless email sign-in link, and the email treatment is kept: request by email address, the same "if an account exists" answer as the password reset, and the link's expired and signed-in states. The technical policies stay unresolved and are not drawn: the link's lifetime, single use, a same-device or same-browser requirement, the request limit, the session it opens, and what happens for an address with no account. AUTH-12 is also P1-L with no reduction listed in section 1.2.

Registration says the address is already registered and offers sign in, a reset and Google. That tells anyone that an account exists for the address, which sign in deliberately avoids (wrong_credentials never says which field is wrong). Nothing contracted forbids it, and the non-disclosing alternative ("Check your email", with a link sent to the existing customer) is noted in the file. Recorded as a security point for the owner; no backend authentication policy is set by the wireframe.

Drawn as shown only after the correct password, so that it reveals nothing to someone without it. That assumes the platform checks the password before the suspension; the order is unverified and is to be confirmed in the build. No backend policy is imposed.

The full-height, full-width drawer is the drawn working treatment at 360 and 390 px. Claude Design recommends keeping it. No new high-fidelity interaction lock is created, and the choice between a drawer and a bottom sheet is not settled.
Kept as drawn: shown after the account is created, where its conditions are met. Its value and conditions are OD-03 variables and stay provisional.
